title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 3)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: Thomas a mal au pi[ed] depuis lundi.
sentences.en: Thomas has had a sore foot since Monday.

sentences.fr: Le m[é]decin demande : « Vous pouv[ez] march[er] ? »
Thomas r[é]pond : « Oui, mais c'est difficile de mont[er] l[es] escali[er]s. »
sentences.en: Thomas answers: "Yes, but it's hard to climb the stairs."

sentences.fr: « Il faut vous repos[er] [et] ne pas jou[er] au hockey cette semaine ! »
sentences.en: "You need to rest and not play hockey this week!"
